newsitem.title: USA: Alabama governor proposes $700 mln highway bonds.
newsitem.headline: Alabama governor proposes $700 mln highway bonds.

text.p: Alabama Gov. Fob James proposed a $700 million bond issue for highways and bridges, with debt service to be paid from existing gasoline taxes.
James introduced the proposal in budget hearings on Tuesday, but formal debate will not begin until the legislature convenes on Feb 4.
The bond issue was scaled back from the $1 billion originally proposed by state Transportation Director Jimmy Butts.
Bond proceeds would finance bypass construction around north Birmingham, south Montgomery and south Huntsville and enable the state to expand several busy highways to four lanes.
The bond issue would give each county $1 million for local road work, and provide $10 million each for the Patton Island Bridge and the Tuscaloosa River Bridge.
State officials estimate debt service would total $1.2 billion over the 25-year life of the bonds.
Alabama issued $185 million of highway bonds in 1984. That debt is scheduled to be retired next year.
James' finance director, Sage Lyons, told lawmakers the state will end fiscal 1997 with its general fund "in very good condition."

He said the general fund budget would approach $1 billion for fiscal 1998 but urged caution because much of that comes from interest on investments and deposits, which could suffer if a strengthening dollar drives interest rates down.
